topics.title: Refraction, Dispersion and Colour
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: understand that light may be refracted as it passes from one medium to another and that this has both consequences and uses (u, s, v/a)
know that white light can be split into coloured light by refraction (k, s)
know that white light results from the superimposition of light of all colours of the visible spectrum (u, k)

body.text: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium into another — for example from air into glass or water — caused by a change in the speed of light between the two media. This is why a straight stick appears to bend at the point where it enters water.

White light, like sunlight, is actually a mixture of all the colours of the visible spectrum — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet — superimposed together. Because each colour refracts by a slightly different amount, a glass prism can split (disperse) white light into its separate colours, spreading them out into a spectrum. A rainbow forms in a similar way, as sunlight is refracted and dispersed by tiny water droplets in the air.
Use the PhET Bending Light simulation below (Prisms screen). Shine white light through a glass prism and watch it split into a spectrum of colours.
